chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it, said, He (peace be upon him) said:
Whenever you plant a tree or vegetation, so recite upon every twig or seed, 'Glorious is the Resurrector, the Inheritor', so it would almost never be wrong, Allah Willing.

key_terms.سُبْحَانَ الْبَاعِثِ الْوَارِثِ: Glorious is the Resurrector, the Inheritor (a specific dhikr)

ai.seo_question: What supplication should be recited when planting a tree or seed in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Shia practice of infusing daily agricultural labor with spiritual remembrance, specifically invoking Allah as 'Al-Ba'ith' (The Resurrector) and 'Al-Warith' (The Inheritor) to connect the growth of plants with the concept of resurrection. The promise that it 'rarely errs' underscores the efficacy of this specific dhikr in ensuring the success of the cultivation, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interconnection between the physical and spiritual realms. This practice serves as a tangible reminder of divine providence and the transient nature of worldly possessions, which ultimately return to Allah.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, raising it, said, 
‘He<sup>asws</sup> said:
‘Whenever you plant a tree or vegetation, so recite upon every twig or seed, ‘Glorious is the Resurrector, the Inheritor’, so it would almost never be wrong, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Willing’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from in a marfu’ manner the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
When you plant a tree or plantation, say with every twig or deed, “Free of all defect is One who raises and inherits”, it then cannot fail, by the will of Allah.’”
